requirement:
Each `AgentConfig` variant carries the corresponding settings from
`trust_but_verify::agent`. Serde uses the `backend` field to select `bedrock`,
`openai`, or `ollama` and reads the settings from the same object.

Choose [`BedrockConfig`](#habeas-req-requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.BedrockConfig),
[`OpenAiConfig`](#habeas-req-requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.OpenAiConfig), or
[`OllamaConfig`](#habeas-req-requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.OllamaConfig) for the selected backend.
With settings omitted, OpenAI uses `gpt-6.1-sol`, `https://api.openai.com/v1`,
and `OPENAI_API_KEY`. Ollama defaults to `http://localhost:11434`.

All three backend constructors start with an empty `options` map. Calling
`option(key, value)` inserts one inference setting. Calling it again with the
same key replaces its value and preserves the other settings. An `OptionValue` is
a `String`, `Boolean`, `Integer(i64)`, `Float(f64)`, `Array`, or `Map`. Arrays hold
option values and maps associate strings with option values. These serialize as
the corresponding untagged values. Backend calls reject nonfinite floats,
including those nested in an array or map.

`BedrockCredentials` contains `access_key_id` and `secret_access_key`, both
`SecretString`, and an optional `session_token` of the same type. Construct a
`SecretString` from `String` or `&str`. `expose_secret()` borrows its value.
Serialization preserves the string, while `Debug` prints `<redacted>`.
rationale:
The reviewed tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/config.rs` cover each obligation of `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.agent_config.settings`. All of them are marked {test} for it.

- **Serde `backend` selection and settings in the same object:** `mod[tests]/fn[all_backends_preserve_nested_settings_and_credentials]` round-trips bedrock, openai and ollama objects with settings, credentials and nested options. It checks that the serialized value equals the input and that a JSON string round trip is equal. `mod[tests]/fn[openai_inference_options_only_fill_missing_defaults]` deserializes `{"backend":"openai"}`.
- **Defaults:**
  - `mod[tests]/fn[option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic]` asserts the OpenAI model `gpt-6.1-sol`, the OpenAI endpoint `https://api.openai.com/v1` and the Ollama endpoint `http://localhost:11434`.
  - `mod[tests]/fn[openai_uses_the_default_credential_variable]` re-runs itself in a child process with `OPENAI_API_KEY` set. It asserts that the default key resolves to the value in that variable.
- **Constructors and `option()`:** `mod[tests]/fn[backend_builders_set_only_the_requested_fields]` covers the constructors of all three backends. It shows no options after construction. It then calls `option` for `a`, `b` and `a` again on all three. The result is `{a:2,b:true}`, so the replacement works and the other key is kept.
- **`OptionValue`:**
  - The round-trip test covers `String`, `Integer`, `Float`, `Boolean`, nested `Array` and nested `Map` as untagged values.
  - `option_defaults_and_credential_resolution_are_deterministic` checks that `1` deserializes to `Integer` and `1.0` to `Float`.
- **Nonfinite floats:** `options_json` is shared by all variants and validates each option value. The tests reject an infinity nested in a map through `OptionValue::validate`. They reject a NaN nested in an array through `AgentConfig::Ollama(..).options_json()`. A top-level nonfinite float uses the same `Float` branch of `validate`, so it needs no separate test.
- **`BedrockCredentials` and `SecretString`:**
  - `backend_builders_set_only_the_requested_fields` covers the credential fields and the optional `session_token`, both absent and present.
  - `mod[tests]/fn[configuration_debug_hides_credentials]` covers construction from `&str` and `String`, `expose_secret`, `Debug` printing `<redacted>`, and serialization preserving the string.

The assertions check the required outcomes, and I found no requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.
